title: Ancient Indian History
summary: From the Harappan cities to the Cholas: sites and finds, Vedic texts, Buddhism & Jainism, Mauryas, Guptas, Harsha and the southern dynasties. SSC asks 1–2 direct fact questions per shift — mostly pairings (site–find, council–king, book–author, dynasty–capital), so tables and mnemonics give quick marks.

subtopics.title: Indus Valley (Harappan) Civilisation
subtopics.concept: The Harappan civilisation is India's oldest city culture. It used copper and bronze but no iron. Its towns had grid streets, covered drains and burnt bricks. Exams ask which site is famous for which find, where each site lies, and who dug it.

tricks.title: Four corners: Many Donkeys Are Slow
tricks.body: **M**anda is north. **D**aimabad is south. **A**lamgirpur is east. **S**utkagendor is west.

example.q: The easternmost Harappan site is:
steps: Use the line: Many Donkeys Are Slow.
The third word gives east: Alamgirpur.

tricks.title: One site, one find
tricks.body: **Lothal** is the dockyard. **Kalibangan** is the ploughed field. **Mohenjo-daro** is the Great Bath. **Chanhudaro** is the bead workshop. **Dholavira** is the water reservoirs.

mistakes.wrong: Swapping the rivers: Harappa on the Indus, Mohenjo-daro on the Ravi.
mistakes.right: Harappa is on the **Ravi**. Mohenjo-daro is on the **Indus**.

mistakes.wrong: Mixing Kalibangan and Banawali.
mistakes.right: Ploughed **field** is Kalibangan. Clay plough **model** is Banawali.

mistakes.wrong: Calling Mohenjo-daro the largest site in India.
mistakes.right: Mohenjo-daro and Harappa are in Pakistan. The largest site in India is **Rakhigarhi**.

mistakes.wrong: Saying Harappans used iron.
mistakes.right: They used copper, bronze, gold and silver. **Iron was unknown**.

mistakes.wrong: Choosing sun-dried bricks for the cities.
mistakes.right: The cities used **burnt** bricks in the ratio 1 : 2 : 4.

subtopics.notes:
### How it was found
Harappa was dug first, in **1921**, by **Daya Ram Sahni**. It lies on the **Ravi** in Punjab, Pakistan.

**Mohenjo-daro** ("mound of the dead") was dug in **1922** by **R.D. Banerji**. It lies on the **Indus** in Sindh.

**Sir John Marshall** announced the new civilisation in 1924. Because Harappa came first, the correct name is the **Harappan civilisation**.

| Point | Fact |
|---|---|
| Age | Bronze Age (copper and tin) |
| Iron | **Not known** |
| Mature phase | About **2600 to 1900 BCE** |
| Script | Picture signs, still **undeciphered** |

### How the cities were built
Every big city followed one plan. This plan is the most asked fact.

- A raised **citadel** stood in the **west**. It held the rulers' buildings and granaries.
- The **lower town** lay in the **east**. Ordinary people lived there.
- Streets crossed at **right angles**. This is a **grid pattern**.
- Drains ran along the streets and were **covered**.
- Bricks were **burnt**. Their ratio was **1 : 2 : 4**.

> **Tip:** Say "citadel west, town east". Do not reverse it.

The **Great Bath** of Mohenjo-daro is a public tank with steps on two sides. Its lining is waterproof bitumen. The **Great Granary** stood nearby.

### Sites and their finds
Learn each site with its one famous find.

| Site | River and place | Famous find |
|---|---|---|
| **Harappa** | Ravi, Punjab (Pakistan) | Rows of granaries, Cemetery R-37 |
| **Mohenjo-daro** | Indus, Sindh (Pakistan) | Great Bath, Dancing Girl, Pashupati seal |
| **Chanhudaro** | Indus, Sindh | Bead-making workshop; **no citadel** |
| **Lothal** | Bhogava, Gujarat | **Dockyard**, rice husk, fire altars |
| **Kalibangan** | Ghaggar, Rajasthan | **Ploughed field**, fire altars |
| **Banawali** | Ghaggar, Haryana | Clay **plough model**, barley |
| **Dholavira** | Kutch, Gujarat | **Water reservoirs**, 10-letter signboard |
| **Rakhigarhi** | Ghaggar plain, Haryana | **Largest site in India** |
| **Surkotada** | Kutch, Gujarat | Horse bones |
| **Ropar** | Sutlej, Punjab | First site dug after Independence |

> **Watch:** A ploughed **field** is Kalibangan. A clay plough **model** is Banawali.

### The four far corners
| Direction | Site | Place |
|---|---|---|
| North | **Manda** | Chenab, J&K |
| South | **Daimabad** | Pravara, Maharashtra (bronze chariot) |
| East | **Alamgirpur** | Hindon, UP |
| West | **Sutkagendor** | Dasht, Baluchistan |

The memory line is "**M**any **D**onkeys **A**re **S**low". It gives north, south, east, west.

### Who dug which site
| Site | Excavator |
|---|---|
| Harappa | Daya Ram Sahni (1921) |
| Mohenjo-daro | R.D. Banerji (1922) |
| Chanhudaro | N.G. Majumdar (1931) |
| Lothal | S.R. Rao (1954 to 55) |
| Ropar | Y.D. Sharma (1953 to 55) |
| Kalibangan | B.B. Lal and B.K. Thapar (1960s) |
| Dholavira | R.S. Bisht (1990) |

### Farming, trade and craft
- Wheat and barley were the main crops.
- **Cotton** was grown here first. The Greeks later called it *Sindon*.
- Rice husk was found at **Lothal** and **Rangpur**.
- Seals were made of **steatite**. The commonest animal on them is the **unicorn** bull.
- Craftsmen used copper, bronze, gold and silver.

> **Note:** Horse evidence is weak. Only Surkotada has horse bones.

### Belief and script
No temple has been found at any site. People honoured a **Mother Goddess**. A seal shows a cross-legged figure among animals, called **Pashupati** (proto-Shiva). The pipal tree was also sacred. The script runs right to left and nobody can read it.

patterns.name: Harappan site and its signature find
patterns.howToSpot: The question names a find (dockyard, Great Bath, ploughed field, bead workshop) and asks for the site. Or it gives a site and asks for the find.
steps: Recall the one-site-one-find table.
Watch near pairs: field is Kalibangan, plough model is Banawali.
Great Bath is Mohenjo-daro. Rows of granaries are Harappa.
Cut the options whose famous find you already know.
patterns.why: Exam setters use the same pairs every year, so one table covers most questions.

example.q: The Harappan site famous for a bead-making workshop, and the only major city without a citadel, is:
steps: Beads point to Chanhudaro.
Chanhudaro is in Sindh, Pakistan.

patterns.name: Site with state or river, and the four corners
patterns.howToSpot: "In which state is", "the northernmost or easternmost site", or a site-to-river match.
steps: First split the sites into Pakistan and India.
Pakistan: Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Chanhudaro, Kot Diji, Sutkagendor.
India by state: Gujarat (Lothal, Dholavira, Surkotada), Haryana (Rakhigarhi, Banawali), Rajasthan (Kalibangan), Punjab (Ropar), UP (Alamgirpur), Maharashtra (Daimabad).
For the corners use Manda, Daimabad, Alamgirpur, Sutkagendor.
patterns.why: Sorting by country and state first removes half the options.

example.q: Which Harappan site lies in Hanumangarh district of Rajasthan, on the dry Ghaggar river?
steps: Rajasthan and Ghaggar point to Kalibangan.
Its name means "black bangles".

patterns.name: Excavator and year
patterns.howToSpot: "Who excavated", "discovered in which year", "first site dug after Independence".
steps: Anchor the dates: Harappa 1921, Mohenjo-daro 1922, announcement 1924.
Match the excavator to the site, not to the whole civilisation.
Later digs: Ropar 1953, Lothal 1954 to 55, Kalibangan 1960s, Dholavira 1990.
patterns.why: The early dates and names are asked most often, so anchor them first.

example.q: Mohenjo-daro was excavated in 1922 by:
steps: Harappa (1921) was dug by Daya Ram Sahni.
Mohenjo-daro was dug the next year by another officer.

patterns.name: Town plan, materials and economy
patterns.howToSpot: Statement questions on burnt bricks, grid plans, drains, seals, crops or metals.
steps: Plan: grid streets, covered drains, citadel west, lower town east.
Bricks: burnt, ratio 1 : 2 : 4.
Economy: wheat and barley, first cotton, steatite seals, unicorn bull.
Metals: copper, bronze, gold, silver. Never iron.
patterns.why: Most wrong statements swap one fact, such as burnt bricks for sun-dried bricks.

example.q:
Statements on Harappan town planning:
1. Streets crossed at right angles in a grid.
2. Houses were built mainly of sun-dried bricks.
3. The citadel lay in the west and the lower town in the east.
Which are correct?
steps: Statement 1 is true.
Statement 2 is false. The bricks were burnt.
Statement 3 is true.

patterns.name: Religion, script and society
patterns.howToSpot: Mother Goddess, Pashupati seal, undeciphered script, burial, or "which is NOT found".
steps: Remember: no temples have been found.
Worship: Mother Goddess, Pashupati seal, pipal tree.
Script: picture signs, right to left, undeciphered.
In "NOT found" questions, pick a Vedic god or a temple.
patterns.why: The civilisation is known only from objects, so the questions test what objects exist.

example.q:
Which of these has NOT been found at Harappan sites?
(a) Mother Goddess figurines (b) A proto-Shiva seal (c) Temple structures (d) Pipal-tree motifs
steps: Figurines, seal and pipal motifs are all known.
No temple building has been found.

patterns.name: Odd one out or record holder
patterns.howToSpot: "Largest site in India", "only city without a citadel", "first dug after Independence", "UNESCO site".
steps: List the record holders: Rakhigarhi largest, Chanhudaro no citadel, Ropar first after Independence, Dholavira UNESCO (2021).
Match the record to the site.
Drop options that are in Pakistan if the question says "in India".
patterns.why: Record titles belong to one site each, so they make easy marks.

example.q:
Which Harappan site in India is the largest?
(a) Lothal (b) Rakhigarhi (c) Kalibangan (d) Ropar
steps: Rakhigarhi is in Hisar district, Haryana.
It is the largest Harappan site in India.

revision: Harappa 1921 (Daya Ram Sahni). Mohenjo-daro 1922 (R.D. Banerji). Announced by John Marshall in 1924.
Bronze Age, no iron. Burnt bricks 1 : 2 : 4. Grid streets and covered drains.
Citadel in the west, lower town in the east.
Lothal is the dockyard. Kalibangan is the ploughed field. Dholavira has water reservoirs.
Corners: Manda north, Daimabad south, Alamgirpur east, Sutkagendor west.
Rakhigarhi is the largest site in India. The unicorn bull is the commonest seal animal.
No temples found. Mother Goddess and Pashupati seal. Script undeciphered.

subtopics.title: Vedic Age & Vedic Literature
subtopics.concept: The Vedic age is named after the Vedas, our main source. Early Vedic life was pastoral and lived around the Punjab rivers. Later Vedic life used iron, farmed the Ganga-Yamuna doab and had rigid varnas. Exams ask about the four Vedas, Rigveda mandalas, river names, the Upanishads and the six schools.

tricks.title: Punjab rivers: Very Angry Parrots Visit Sutlej
tricks.body: **V**itasta is Jhelum, **A**sikni is Chenab, **P**arushni is Ravi, **V**ipas is Beas, **S**utudri is Sutlej. Modern order: J-C-R-B-S.

example.q: The Rigvedic river Asikni is today's:
steps: Asikni is second in the chain V-A-P-V-S.
Second in J-C-R-B-S is Chenab.

tricks.title: Veda and priest: HUAB
tricks.body: **H**otri with Rig, **U**dgatri with Sama, **A**dhvaryu with Yajur, **B**rahma with Atharva.

tricks.title: Mandalas 3-7-9-10
tricks.body: **3** Gayatri. **7** Ten Kings. **9** Soma. **10** Purusha Sukta.

mistakes.wrong: Saying the Gayatri Mantra is to a goddess Gayatri.
mistakes.right: It is addressed to **Savitri**, the sun god, in Mandala **III**.

mistakes.wrong: Saying "Satyameva Jayate" comes from the Rigveda.
mistakes.right: It comes from the **Mundaka** Upanishad.

mistakes.wrong: Treating the most-mentioned river and the holiest river as one.
mistakes.right: Most mentioned is the **Sindhu**. Holiest is the **Saraswati**.

mistakes.wrong: Placing iron in the Early Vedic period.
mistakes.right: Iron appears only in the **Later** Vedic period.

subtopics.notes:
### Two halves of one age
The Vedic age runs from about **1500 to 600 BCE**. It has two phases.

| Point | Early Vedic (1500 to 1000 BCE) | Later Vedic (1000 to 600 BCE) |
|---|---|---|
| Region | **Sapta Sindhu** (land of seven rivers) | **Ganga-Yamuna doab** |
| Economy | Cattle herding; cattle were wealth | Farming; **iron** appears |
| Pottery | Ochre and plain grey | **Painted Grey Ware** |
| Women | Better position; Sabha was open to them | Position falls; child marriage appears |
| Assemblies | Sabha, Samiti, Vidatha all active | They lose power to the king |
| Officers | Rajan, Purohita, Senani, Gramani | Add Bhagadugha (tax collector), Sangrahitri (treasurer) |
| Bali | Voluntary gift | Regular tax |
| Varna | Flexible | Rigid; gotra exogamy rule |

Iron was called *shyama ayas* or *krishna ayas*, meaning "dark metal".

### The four Vedas
| Veda | Content | Priest |
|---|---|---|
| **Rigveda** | Oldest; 10 mandalas, 1028 hymns | Hotri |
| **Samaveda** | Rigvedic hymns set to melody; root of Indian music | Udgatri |
| **Yajurveda** | Sacrificial formulas in prose and verse | Adhvaryu |
| **Atharvaveda** | Charms, spells, folk medicine | Brahma |

> **Tip:** Say "Rig-Hotri, Sama-Udgatri, Yajur-Adhvaryu, Atharva-Brahma".

Each Veda has later layers: **Brahmanas** (ritual prose), then **Aranyakas** (forest texts), then **Upanishads** (philosophy). Aitareya goes with the Rigveda. Shatapatha goes with the Yajurveda.

The six Vedangas are Shiksha, Kalpa, Vyakarana, Nirukta, Chhanda and Jyotisha.

### Rigveda anchors
Four mandalas are asked again and again.

| Mandala | Content |
|---|---|
| **III** | **Gayatri Mantra**, to **Savitri**, by **Vishwamitra** |
| **VII** | **Battle of Ten Kings** on the Parushni (Ravi); **Sudas** of the Bharatas won |
| **IX** | Wholly to **Soma** |
| **X** | **Purusha Sukta**, the first mention of the four varnas |

**Indra** gets the most hymns (about 250). He is called *Purandara*, the fort-breaker. **Agni** comes next (about 200). **Varuna** guards *rita*, the cosmic order.

The **Sindhu** is the most-named river. The **Saraswati** is the holiest (*naditama*).

> **Watch:** Gayatri Mantra is addressed to Savitri, not to a goddess named Gayatri.

### Rigvedic river names
| Rigvedic | Modern |
|---|---|
| Vitasta | Jhelum |
| Asikni | Chenab |
| Parushni | Ravi |
| Vipas | Beas |
| Sutudri | Sutlej |
| Kubha | Kabul |
| Krumu | Kurram |
| Drishadvati | Ghaggar-Chautang |

The first five run west to east. The modern names follow the same order: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej.

### Terms of polity and ritual
- **Sabha** is the council of elders. **Samiti** is the people's assembly. **Vidatha** is the oldest assembly.
- **Gramani** is the village headman. **Bali** is tribute.
- Later Vedic kings held big sacrifices. **Rajasuya** is a consecration. **Ashvamedha** is a horse sacrifice for supremacy. **Vajapeya** is a chariot race.
- The four ashramas are Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha and Sanyasa. The **Jabala Upanishad** lists all four.

### Upanishads and six schools
| Upanishad | Remember for |
|---|---|
| **Mundaka** | "Satyameva Jayate" |
| **Katha** | Nachiketa and Yama |
| **Brihadaranyaka** | Oldest and largest; Yajnavalkya and Gargi |
| **Chandogya** | Early mention of Krishna, son of Devaki |

| School | Founder |
|---|---|
| Sankhya | Kapila |
| Yoga | Patanjali |
| Nyaya | Gautama (Akshapada) |
| Vaisheshika | Kanada |
| Purva Mimamsa | Jaimini |
| Uttara Mimamsa (Vedanta) | Badarayana |

patterns.name: Veda with priest, upaveda or content
patterns.howToSpot: "Which Veda is called", "the priest who recites the Samaveda", "Dhanurveda belongs to which Veda".
steps: Recall the four Vedas with priests: Rig-Hotri, Sama-Udgatri, Yajur-Adhvaryu, Atharva-Brahma.
Upavedas: Ayurveda-Rig, Gandharvaveda-Sama, Dhanurveda-Yajur, Shilpaveda-Atharva.
Atharvaveda is the Veda of charms and spells.
patterns.why: Each Veda has one fixed set of links, so a table settles every option.

example.q: Which Veda has sacrificial formulas in both prose and verse?
steps: Prose and verse together points to one Veda.
It has Shukla (white) and Krishna (black) forms.

patterns.name: Rigveda mandala and hymn facts
patterns.howToSpot: Gayatri Mantra, Battle of Ten Kings, Soma, Purusha Sukta, "most hymns to which god".
steps: Anchor: 3 Gayatri, 7 Ten Kings, 9 Soma, 10 Purusha Sukta.
Most hymns: Indra (about 250), then Agni (about 200).
Ten Kings: river Parushni (Ravi), winner Sudas of the Bharatas.
patterns.why: Only four mandalas are asked, so memorise those four.

example.q: The Gayatri Mantra of the Rigveda was composed by:
steps: It is in Mandala III.
The composer is Vishwamitra.

patterns.name: Rigvedic river and modern name
patterns.howToSpot: A Rigvedic river name with modern rivers as options, or the reverse.
steps: Learn the chain west to east: Vitasta, Asikni, Parushni, Vipas, Sutudri.
Match it with Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej.
Extras: Kubha Kabul, Krumu Kurram, Drishadvati Ghaggar-Chautang.
patterns.why: The two chains run in the same order, so one list gives the other.

example.q: The Rigvedic river Vitasta is known today as:
steps: Vitasta is first in the west-to-east chain.
The first modern name is Jhelum.

patterns.name: Early and Later Vedic life and terms
patterns.howToSpot: A comparison of early and later Vedic society, or one term such as Bali, Vidatha, PGW.
steps: Note the direction of change: cattle to farming, Sapta Sindhu to doab.
Assemblies weaken and kings gain power.
Bali moves from voluntary gift to tax.
Iron and Painted Grey Ware belong to the Later Vedic age.
patterns.why: Every later change points one way, so you can guess the direction.

example.q: In the Rigvedic period, Bali was:
steps: Bali is a payment to the chief.
In Rigvedic times it was voluntary.
example.answer: A voluntary tribute to the chief

patterns.name: Upanishad and school of philosophy
patterns.howToSpot: "Satyameva Jayate is taken from", "founder of the Nyaya school", "Nachiketa appears in".
steps: Upanishads: Mundaka Satyameva Jayate, Katha Nachiketa, Brihadaranyaka oldest, Chandogya Krishna.
Founders: Sankhya Kapila, Yoga Patanjali, Nyaya Gautama, Vaisheshika Kanada, Mimamsa Jaimini, Vedanta Badarayana.
All six schools accept the Vedas as authority.
patterns.why: There are only four Upanishads and six founders to learn.

example.q: The Vaisheshika school, known for its atomic theory, was founded by:
steps: Vaisheshika teaches atoms.
Its founder is Kanada.

patterns.name: Sacrifices, ashramas and later Vedic terms
patterns.howToSpot: "Horse sacrifice", "chariot race", "four ashramas", "Vedangas".
steps: Rajasuya is consecration, Ashvamedha is horse sacrifice, Vajapeya is chariot race.
Ashramas: Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha, Sanyasa (Jabala Upanishad).
Vedangas: Shiksha, Kalpa, Vyakarana, Nirukta, Chhanda, Jyotisha.
patterns.why: Each term has one plain meaning that the option list repeats.

example.q: The Vajapeya sacrifice of the Later Vedic age was a:
steps: Rajasuya was a consecration.
Ashvamedha was a horse sacrifice.
Vajapeya is the remaining one.

revision: Early Vedic: cattle, Sapta Sindhu, flexible society. Later Vedic: iron, doab, Painted Grey Ware, rigid varna.
Veda and priest: Rig-Hotri, Sama-Udgatri, Yajur-Adhvaryu, Atharva-Brahma.
Mandalas: 3 Gayatri, 7 Ten Kings, 9 Soma, 10 Purusha Sukta.
Rivers: Vitasta Jhelum, Asikni Chenab, Parushni Ravi, Vipas Beas, Sutudri Sutlej.
Satyameva Jayate is from the Mundaka Upanishad. Brihadaranyaka is the oldest Upanishad.
Founders: Kapila, Patanjali, Gautama, Kanada, Jaimini, Badarayana.

subtopics.title: Mahajanapadas & Rise of Magadha
subtopics.concept: By the 6th century BCE north India had sixteen big states called mahajanapadas. Magadha beat the rest and grew into an empire under the Haryanka, Shishunaga and Nanda dynasties. Persian and Greek invaders entered the north-west in the same age. Exams ask for capitals, rulers in order, and the two invasions.

tricks.title: Capital pairs by first letter
tricks.body: **V**atsa-**K**aushambi and **V**ajji-**V**aishali. **A**vanti-Ujjain and **A**nga-Champa. **G**andhara-Taxila. Kuru-Indraprastha.

tricks.title: Magadha order: Hari Shishu Nanda
tricks.body: **Hary**anka, then **Shishu**naga, then **Nanda**, then Maurya. Council 1 is Ajatashatru (Haryanka). Council 2 is Kalashoka (Shishunaga).

example.q: The Second Buddhist Council was held under which dynasty?
steps: Kalashoka held it at Vaishali.
Kalashoka belongs to the Shishunaga dynasty.

mistakes.wrong: Saying Ajatashatru founded Pataliputra.
mistakes.right: **Udayin** founded Pataliputra.

mistakes.wrong: Putting Assaka in the north.
mistakes.right: Assaka is the only mahajanapada **south of the Vindhyas**. Avanti is in Malwa.

mistakes.wrong: Saying Alexander's army mutinied at the Jhelum.
mistakes.right: The battle with Porus was at the **Jhelum**. The mutiny was at the **Beas**.

mistakes.wrong: Mixing up Vatsa and Kosala capitals.
mistakes.right: Vatsa is **Kaushambi**. Kosala is **Shravasti**.

subtopics.notes:
### The sixteen states
The Buddhist text **Anguttara Nikaya** lists **16 mahajanapadas**. The Jain *Bhagavati Sutra* gives a slightly different list.

| Mahajanapada | Capital | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Magadha** | Girivraja (Rajagriha), later Pataliputra | Became the empire |
| Anga | **Champa** | Annexed by Bimbisara |
| Kashi | **Varanasi** | Absorbed by Kosala and Magadha |
| Kosala | **Shravasti** (also Ayodhya) | Eastern UP |
| **Vajji** | **Vaishali** | Republic of 8 clans, including Licchavis |
| **Malla** | **Kushinara**, Pava | Republic |
| Chedi | Shuktimati | Bundelkhand |
| Vatsa | **Kaushambi** | Near Prayagraj |
| Kuru | **Indraprastha** | Delhi-Meerut area |
| Panchala | Ahichchhatra, Kampilya | Western UP |
| Matsya | **Viratnagar** | Jaipur-Alwar area |
| Surasena | **Mathura** | UP |
| **Assaka** | Potana | **Only one south of the Vindhyas** |
| **Avanti** | **Ujjain** (north), Mahishmati (south) | Malwa |
| Gandhara | **Taxila** | North-west |
| Kamboja | Rajapura | Known for horses |

> **Tip:** Learn six pairs first: Avanti-Ujjain, Vatsa-Kaushambi, Kosala-Shravasti, Anga-Champa, Gandhara-Taxila, Matsya-Viratnagar.

Vajji and Malla were **republics**. The others were kingdoms.

### Why Magadha won
Four states were the strongest: **Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa and Avanti**. Magadha won because it had:

- **Iron mines** for weapons and ploughs.
- The rich **Ganga plain**.
- **Elephants** for its army.
- Natural forts at Rajagriha.

### The rulers in order
| Dynasty | Rulers and events |
|---|---|
| **Haryanka** | **Bimbisara**: met both Buddha and Mahavira; made marriage alliances; annexed Anga |
| | **Ajatashatru**: killed his father; fought the Vajjis; **First Buddhist Council** |
| | **Udayin**: founded **Pataliputra** at the Ganga-Son meeting point |
| **Shishunaga** | **Shishunaga**: destroyed **Avanti** |
| | **Kalashoka**: **Second Buddhist Council** at Vaishali |
| **Nanda** | **Mahapadma Nanda**: first non-Kshatriya empire builder; titles *Ekarat* and *Sarvakshatrantaka* |
| | **Dhana Nanda**: last Nanda; met Alexander; overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya |

> **Watch:** Udayin, not Ajatashatru, founded Pataliputra.

### The Persians
**Darius I** took Gandhara and the Punjab about **516 BCE**. Persian contact brought the **Kharosthi** script. It is written right to left.

### Alexander
- **Alexander** invaded in **326 BCE**.
- He beat **Porus (Puru)** at the **Hydaspes (Jhelum)**.
- His tired troops refused to go beyond the **Beas (Hyphasis)**.
- He died at Babylon in **323 BCE**.

> **Watch:** The battle was at the Jhelum. The mutiny was at the Beas.

patterns.name: Mahajanapada and its capital
patterns.howToSpot: A capital or state is given with four options, or "which pair is correctly matched".
steps: Recall the six key pairs.
Republics have cities, not royal capitals: Vajji-Vaishali, Malla-Kushinara.
Magadha had two capitals in turn: Rajagriha, then Pataliputra.
patterns.why: Setters pick pairs from the same short list every year.

example.q: The capital of the Vatsa mahajanapada was:
steps: Vatsa is linked with a city near Prayagraj.
That city is Kaushambi.

patterns.name: Magadhan ruler and event
patterns.howToSpot: "Who founded Pataliputra", "under which dynasty was the Second Council held", or an order of rulers.
steps: Recall the chain: Haryanka, Shishunaga, Nanda.
Attach one event to each king: Bimbisara annexed Anga, Ajatashatru beat the Vajjis, Udayin founded Pataliputra.
Shishunaga destroyed Avanti. Kalashoka held the 2nd Council. Mahapadma Nanda was Ekarat.
patterns.why: Each king has one event, so the event names the king.

example.q: Who founded Pataliputra at the meeting point of the Ganga and the Son?
steps: Ajatashatru is the trap option.
The Haryanka successor Udayin founded the city.

patterns.name: Source text, republics and odd facts
patterns.howToSpot: "The list of 16 mahajanapadas occurs in", "which was a republic", "the only one south of the Vindhyas".
steps: Source: Anguttara Nikaya (Buddhist). The Jain list differs.
Republics: Vajji (with Licchavis) and Malla.
Extremes: Assaka in the south, Kamboja in the north-west with its horses.
patterns.why: Each odd fact points to one state.

example.q: The list of sixteen mahajanapadas appears in which Buddhist text?
steps: The Jain Bhagavati Sutra gives a different list.
The Buddhist list is in the Anguttara Nikaya.

patterns.name: Persian and Alexander's invasions
patterns.howToSpot: Darius I, Kharosthi script, the Hydaspes battle, the Beas mutiny.
steps: Darius I, about 516 BCE: Gandhara and west Punjab. He brought Kharosthi.
Alexander, 326 BCE: beat Porus at the Hydaspes (Jhelum).
The troops refused at the Beas (Hyphasis). He died at Babylon in 323 BCE.
patterns.why: Each event has one river, and the rivers are the traps.

example.q: Alexander's army refused to march beyond which river?
steps: The battle with Porus was at the Jhelum.
The refusal came further east, at the Hyphasis.

patterns.name: Why Magadha rose
patterns.howToSpot: "Which factor helped the rise of Magadha" or "which was NOT a reason".
steps: List the reasons: iron mines, Ganga plain, elephants, natural forts.
Cut any option outside this list.
Remember the rival powers: Kosala, Vatsa, Avanti.
patterns.why: The list of reasons is short, so any new item is the wrong option.

example.q:
Which of these helped Magadha most in its early rise?
(a) Iron mines nearby (b) Sea trade with Rome (c) A large navy (d) Silk Road tolls
steps: Magadha had iron ores in south Bihar.
The other options belong to later or different regions.

patterns.name: Arrange rulers in order
patterns.howToSpot: "Arrange in chronological order" with three or four Magadhan kings.
steps: Write the dynasty next to each king.
Order the dynasties: Haryanka, Shishunaga, Nanda.
Inside Haryanka: Bimbisara, Ajatashatru, Udayin.
patterns.why: Placing the dynasty first gives most of the order.

example.q: Arrange in order: 1. Mahapadma Nanda 2. Bimbisara 3. Udayin 4. Kalashoka
steps: Bimbisara and Udayin are Haryanka, with Bimbisara first.
Kalashoka is Shishunaga.
Mahapadma Nanda is Nanda.

revision: The list of 16 mahajanapadas is in the Anguttara Nikaya (Buddhist).
Capital pairs: Avanti-Ujjain, Vatsa-Kaushambi, Kosala-Shravasti, Anga-Champa, Gandhara-Taxila, Matsya-Viratnagar.
Assaka is the only mahajanapada south of the Vindhyas. Vajji and Malla were republics.
Dynasty chain: Haryanka, Shishunaga, Nanda, Maurya.
Bimbisara, Ajatashatru (1st Council), Udayin (Pataliputra), Shishunaga (ended Avanti), Kalashoka (2nd Council), Mahapadma Nanda, Dhana Nanda.
Darius I brought Kharosthi. Alexander beat Porus at the Jhelum in 326 BCE and turned back at the Beas.

subtopics.title: Buddhism & Jainism
subtopics.concept: Buddhism and Jainism began in the 6th century BCE in the Magadha region. Both preached ahimsa and used the people's language. Exams ask about the Buddha's five life events, the four Buddhist councils, the 24 Tirthankaras and Mahavira's vows.

tricks.title: Councils: places, kings, presidents
tricks.body: Places: **Raj**agriha, **Vaish**ali, **Pat**aliputra, **Kash**mir. Kings: **A**jatashatru, **K**alashoka, **A**shoka, **K**anishka. Presidents: Maha-Saba-Moggali-Vasu.

example.q: Who presided over the Third Buddhist Council?
steps: Third means Pataliputra and Ashoka.
The third name in the chain is Moggaliputta Tissa.

tricks.title: Buddha symbols in order
tricks.body: Birth lotus, renunciation horse, enlightenment tree, first sermon wheel, death stupa.

tricks.title: Tirthankara symbols
tricks.body: Bull begins and lion ends. The 22nd has a conch. The 23rd has a snake.

mistakes.wrong: Saying Mahavira gave all five vows.
mistakes.right: Parshvanatha gave four. Mahavira **added Brahmacharya**.

mistakes.wrong: Mixing Sarnath and Bodh Gaya.
mistakes.right: Enlightenment is at **Bodh Gaya**. First sermon is at **Sarnath**. Death is at **Kushinagar**.

mistakes.wrong: Swapping the splits of the 2nd and 4th councils.
mistakes.right: 2nd: Sthaviravadins and Mahasanghikas. 4th: Hinayana and Mahayana.

mistakes.wrong: Saying the Palas founded Nalanda.
mistakes.right: Nalanda was founded by **Kumaragupta I** of the Guptas. Vikramashila is Pala.

subtopics.notes:
### Why two new faiths rose
Both faiths began in the Magadha-Vaishali belt. Ritual religion had become costly and full of animal sacrifice. Merchants wanted simpler, ethical teaching.

Both preached **ahimsa** and used the people's language. Early Buddhism used **Pali**. Jainism used **Prakrit (Ardhamagadhi)**.

### The Buddha's life
| Event | Place | Symbol |
|---|---|---|
| Birth | **Lumbini** (Nepal) | Lotus and bull |
| Renunciation, age 29 | Left on horse **Kanthaka** with charioteer **Channa** | Horse |
| Enlightenment, age 35 | **Bodh Gaya**, under the Bodhi tree | Bodhi tree |
| First sermon | **Sarnath** (Deer Park) | Wheel |
| Death, age 80 | **Kushinagar** (Malla republic) | Stupa |

He was a **Shakya** prince. His father was Suddhodana and his mother was Mahamaya. His wife was **Yashodhara** and his son was **Rahula**.

> **Tip:** Symbols in order: lotus, horse, tree, wheel, stupa.

### What the Buddha taught
- **Four Noble Truths:** the world has sorrow; desire causes it; it can end; the Eightfold Path ends it.
- **Eightfold Path:** the **Middle Path** between luxury and harsh austerity.
- **Tri-ratna:** Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha.
- **Tripitaka:** *Vinaya* (monastic rules), *Sutta* (talks), *Abhidhamma* (philosophy).
- **Jatakas** are stories of the Buddha's earlier births.

### The four Buddhist Councils
| Council | Place | King | President | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1st, 483 BCE | Rajagriha | Ajatashatru | Mahakassapa | Sutta (Ananda) and Vinaya (Upali) compiled |
| 2nd, 383 BCE | Vaishali | Kalashoka | Sabakami | Split: Sthaviravadins and Mahasanghikas |
| 3rd, 250 BCE | Pataliputra | Ashoka | Moggaliputta Tissa | Abhidhamma added; missions sent |
| 4th, c. 72 CE | Kundalvana, Kashmir | Kanishka | Vasumitra (deputy Ashvaghosha) | Split: Hinayana and Mahayana |

> **Tip:** Places are Raj-Vaish-Pat-Kash. Kings are A-K-A-K.

### Jainism
There are **24 Tirthankaras**.

| No. | Name | Symbol |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Rishabhanatha** (Adinatha) | Bull |
| 22 | Neminatha | Conch |
| 23 | **Parshvanatha** | Snake |
| 24 | **Mahavira** | Lion |

**Parshvanatha** was a prince of Varanasi. He gave **four vows**: ahimsa, satya, asteya, aparigraha.

**Mahavira** was born at **Kundagrama** near Vaishali. He gained **kaivalya** at 42 and died at **Pavapuri** at 72. He **added the fifth vow, Brahmacharya**. His titles were *Jina* and *Nirgrantha*.

The Jain **tri-ratna** is right faith, right knowledge and right conduct.

- **Sects:** Digambara (sky-clad, led by Bhadrabahu) and Shvetambara (white-clad, Sthulabhadra).
- **Councils:** first at Pataliputra (c. 300 BCE), second at Vallabhi (Gujarat, 5th to 6th century CE).

### Texts and monuments
- **Milindapanha:** dialogue of Menander (Milinda) and the monk Nagasena.
- **Nagarjuna** was a Mahayana philosopher of the Madhyamika school.
- **Gommateshwara (Bahubali)** statue, Shravanabelagola, Karnataka, c. 983 CE, built by Chamundaraya.
- **Dilwara** Jain temples, Mount Abu.
- **Nalanda:** founded by Kumaragupta I. **Vikramashila:** Dharmapala. **Odantapuri:** Gopala.

> **Watch:** Nalanda is Gupta. Vikramashila is Pala.

patterns.name: Buddha's life event, place and symbol
patterns.howToSpot: "Where did the Buddha attain enlightenment", "symbol of Mahaparinirvana", or an order of life events.
steps: Recall the chain: Lumbini, renunciation at 29, Bodh Gaya at 35, Sarnath, Kushinagar at 80.
Recall the symbols: lotus, horse, tree, wheel, stupa.
Extras: horse Kanthaka, charioteer Channa, wife Yashodhara, son Rahula.
patterns.why: Five events with five places and five symbols cover the whole topic.

example.q: Where did Gautama Buddha attain Mahaparinirvana?
steps: Death is the last event in the chain.
It took place in the Malla republic.

patterns.name: Buddhist council with place, king, president, result
patterns.howToSpot: "The Fourth Council was held under", "which council added the Abhidhamma", council-president pairs.
steps: Places: Rajagriha, Vaishali, Pataliputra, Kashmir.
Kings: Ajatashatru, Kalashoka, Ashoka, Kanishka.
Presidents: Mahakassapa, Sabakami, Moggaliputta Tissa, Vasumitra.
Results: 2nd first split, 3rd Abhidhamma, 4th Hinayana and Mahayana.
patterns.why: One table of four rows gives every answer.

example.q: Which Buddhist council led to the split into Hinayana and Mahayana?
steps: Hinayana and Mahayana is the last split.
It was held in Kashmir under Kanishka.
example.answer: The Fourth Council (c. 72 CE), president Vasumitra, deputy Ashvaghosha

patterns.name: Tirthankaras, Mahavira and the vows
patterns.howToSpot: "Who was the 23rd Tirthankara", "which vow was added by Mahavira", "kaivalya at the age of".
steps: Numbers: 1 Rishabha (bull), 22 Neminatha (conch), 23 Parshvanatha (snake), 24 Mahavira (lion).
Mahavira: Kundagrama, kaivalya at 42, death at Pavapuri at 72.
Parshva gave four vows. Mahavira added Brahmacharya.
patterns.why: The number, symbol and vow facts are the whole question bank.

example.q: Which vow did Mahavira add to the four preached by Parshvanatha?
steps: The four old vows were ahimsa, satya, asteya, aparigraha.
The new vow concerns celibacy.

patterns.name: Texts, sects and monuments
patterns.howToSpot: "Milindapanha is a dialogue between", "Gommateshwara is at", "Vikramashila was founded by".
steps: Texts: Tripitaka, Jatakas, Milindapanha (Menander and Nagasena).
Jain monuments: Gommateshwara at Shravanabelagola, Dilwara at Mount Abu.
Monasteries: Nalanda (Kumaragupta I), Vikramashila (Dharmapala), Odantapuri (Gopala).
patterns.why: Each text or place has one name attached.

example.q: The Milindapanha records a dialogue between the monk Nagasena and which king?
steps: The king is an Indo-Greek.
His Indian name is Milinda.

patterns.name: Teachings and tri-ratna
patterns.howToSpot: "Tri-ratna of Buddhism", "Middle Path", "Four Noble Truths", "Jain tri-ratna".
steps: Buddhist tri-ratna: Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha.
Jain tri-ratna: right faith, right knowledge, right conduct.
Middle Path is the Eightfold Path.
patterns.why: The two tri-ratnas differ, and setters swap them.

example.q:
Which of these is the Jain tri-ratna?
(a) Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha (b) Right faith, right knowledge, right conduct (c) Ahimsa, satya, asteya (d) Sutta, Vinaya, Abhidhamma
steps: Option (a) is the Buddhist tri-ratna.
Option (d) is the Tripitaka.
example.answer: (b) Right faith, right knowledge, right conduct

patterns.name: Jain sects and councils
patterns.howToSpot: "Digambara", "Shvetambara", "Vallabhi", "12 Angas", "Bhadrabahu".
steps: Digambara: sky-clad, led by Bhadrabahu.
Shvetambara: white-clad, Sthulabhadra.
First council at Pataliputra (12 Angas). Second at Vallabhi, where the canon was written.
patterns.why: Two sects and two councils make a small table.

example.q: The second Jain council, where the canon was written down, was held at:
steps: The first council was at Pataliputra.
The second was in Gujarat.

revision: Life chain: Lumbini, Bodh Gaya, Sarnath, Kushinagar. Symbols: lotus, horse, tree, wheel, stupa.
Councils: Rajagriha, Vaishali, Pataliputra, Kashmir. Kings A-K-A-K. Presidents Maha-Saba-Moggali-Vasu.
2nd council: first split. 3rd: Abhidhamma. 4th: Hinayana and Mahayana.
Tirthankaras: 1 bull, 22 conch, 23 snake (four vows), 24 lion (added Brahmacharya).
Jain sects: Digambara and Shvetambara. Councils at Pataliputra and Vallabhi.
Gommateshwara is at Shravanabelagola. Nalanda is Kumaragupta I. Vikramashila is Dharmapala.

subtopics.title: Mauryan Empire
subtopics.concept: The Mauryas built the first empire that covered almost all India. Chandragupta founded it and Ashoka is its most famous king. Ashoka's edicts on rocks and pillars are our main source. Exams ask about rulers, edicts, officers, Greek visitors and Mauryan art.

tricks.title: Edict numbers: 2, 5, 12, 13
tricks.body: **2** hospital ward. **5** officer rank. **12** faiths tolerated. **13** the unlucky war.

example.q: Which Major Rock Edict records Ashoka's remorse after Kalinga?
steps: Use the number line: 13 is the war.
13 is Kalinga.

tricks.title: Dynasty start dates: 322, 185, 73
tricks.body: Maurya begins in **322** BCE. Shunga begins in **185** BCE. Kanva begins in **73** BCE.

mistakes.wrong: Saying Megasthenes and Deimachus served the same court.
mistakes.right: Megasthenes served Seleucus at Chandragupta's court. Deimachus served Antiochus I at Bindusara's court.

mistakes.wrong: Mixing the faiths of the three kings.
mistakes.right: Chandragupta ended as a **Jain**. Bindusara followed **Ajivikas**. Ashoka became **Buddhist**.

mistakes.wrong: Saying the Major Rock Edicts name "Ashoka".
mistakes.right: They use **Devanampiya Piyadasi**. The name Ashoka appears in **Maski**.

mistakes.wrong: Saying John Marshall deciphered Brahmi.
mistakes.right: **James Prinsep** deciphered Brahmi in 1837.

subtopics.notes:
### The rulers
| Ruler | Reign | Key facts |
|---|---|---|
| **Chandragupta Maurya** | 322 to 298 BCE | Overthrew Dhana Nanda with **Chanakya (Kautilya)**; faced **Seleucus Nicator** in 305 BCE |
| **Bindusara** | 298 to 273 BCE | Title **Amitraghata** ("slayer of foes"); followed the **Ajivika** sect |
| **Ashoka** | c. 268 to 232 BCE | **Kalinga war, 261 BCE**; turned to Buddhism; *Dhamma* policy |
| **Brihadratha** | Last king | Killed by **Pushyamitra Shunga** in 185 BCE |

In the treaty of 305 BCE Seleucus received **500 war elephants**. Chandragupta received the eastern satrapies and a marriage alliance. The Greeks called him **Sandrocottus**.

Late in life Chandragupta became a Jain. He went to **Shravanabelagola** with **Bhadrabahu**.

### Foreign visitors and books
- **Megasthenes** came from Seleucus to Chandragupta's court. His book **Indica** survives only in fragments.
- **Deimachus** came to Bindusara from Antiochus I.
- The **Arthashastra** by Kautilya is a book on statecraft with 15 books (*adhikaranas*).

> **Watch:** Megasthenes served Seleucus. Deimachus served Antiochus I.

### Ashoka and Dhamma
The Kalinga war of **261 BCE** was in Ashoka's 8th regnal year. The bloodshed made him turn to **Dhamma**. Dhamma is a code of conduct, not a new religion. It means tolerance, ahimsa, kindness to servants and animals, and respect for all sects.

He held the **Third Buddhist Council**. He called himself **Devanampiya Piyadasi** (beloved of the gods).

### Ashoka's edicts
| Type | Facts |
|---|---|
| **Major Rock Edicts** (14) | **RE II** medical care; **RE V** Dhamma Mahamattas; **RE XII** tolerance; **RE XIII** Kalinga war and remorse |
| **Kalinga Edicts** | Dhauli and Jaugada, Odisha: "All men are my children" |
| **Minor Rock Edicts** | **Maski** names the king as "Ashoka" |
| **Bhabru edict** | Faith in Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha |
| **Rummindei pillar** | Visit to Lumbini |
| **Pillar Edicts** (7) | Delhi-Topra pillar has all seven |

- Language is **Prakrit**. Script is mostly **Brahmi**.
- **Kharosthi** is used at Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra. **Greek and Aramaic** are used at Kandahar.
- **James Prinsep** deciphered Brahmi in **1837**.

> **Tip:** Edict numbers: 2 hospital, 5 officers, 12 tolerance, 13 Kalinga.

### How the empire was run
| Officer | Job |
|---|---|
| **Samaharta** | Chief revenue collector |
| **Sannidhata** | Treasurer and storekeeper |
| **Gudhapurusha** | Spies |
| **Kumara** | Prince governing a province |

Provinces included Taxila, Ujjain, Tosali and Suvarnagiri. The usual land tax was **one-sixth** (*bhaga*). Megasthenes said Pataliputra was run by **6 committees of 5 members**.

### Art and the end
- **Sarnath Lion Capital** became the **National Emblem** on **26 January 1950**. Its shaft is polished **Chunar sandstone**.
- **Barabar caves** in Bihar were cut for the **Ajivikas**.
- **Didarganj Yakshi** is a fly-whisk bearer, now in the Patna Museum.
- After weak later kings, **Brihadratha** was killed by his general **Pushyamitra Shunga** in **185 BCE**.

patterns.name: Which edict says what
patterns.howToSpot: "Which edict describes the Kalinga war", "where does the name Ashoka appear", script or language questions.
steps: Anchor: RE XIII Kalinga, RE XII tolerance, Bhabru Buddha-Dhamma-Sangha, Rummindei Lumbini.
The name Ashoka appears in Minor Rock Edicts such as Maski. Elsewhere he is Devanampiya Piyadasi.
Script: Brahmi mostly, Kharosthi in the north-west, Greek and Aramaic at Kandahar.
patterns.why: Each edict has one theme and one site.

example.q: Which Ashokan edict records the king's faith in the Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha?
steps: The message is about faith in the three jewels.
It was found near Jaipur.

patterns.name: Mauryan officers and machinery
patterns.howToSpot: "Who was the Samaharta", spy wings, provincial governors, Dhamma Mahamattas.
steps: Samaharta collects revenue. Sannidhata is the treasurer.
Provinces were held by Kumara princes.
Spies are gudhapurushas.
patterns.why: Job titles come in pairs, so learn them as pairs.

example.q: In Mauryan administration, the officer who collected revenue was the:
steps: The treasurer was the Sannidhata.
The collector is the other officer.

patterns.name: Chandragupta, Chanakya and the Greeks
patterns.howToSpot: The founding of the empire, the Arthashastra, the Seleucus treaty, Indica.
steps: 322 BCE: Chandragupta and Kautilya end Dhana Nanda.
305 BCE treaty: 500 elephants for the eastern satrapies and a marriage alliance.
Visitors: Megasthenes at Chandragupta's court and Deimachus at Bindusara's.
patterns.why: The treaty terms and the visitors are asked in almost every paper.

example.q: Under the Mauryan treaty with Seleucus in 305 BCE, Chandragupta gave Seleucus:
steps: Seleucus received animals for war.
The number was 500.

patterns.name: Art, architecture and the end of the dynasty
patterns.howToSpot: Lion Capital, Barabar caves, polished pillars, Brihadratha and Pushyamitra.
steps: Polished Chunar sandstone pillars. Lion Capital is the National Emblem.
Barabar caves were cut for the Ajivikas.
Brihadratha was killed in 185 BCE by Pushyamitra Shunga.
patterns.why: Each art item has one link, and the end date is fixed.

example.q: The Barabar hill caves of the Mauryan age were given to which sect?
steps: Bindusara followed this sect.
The sect is the Ajivikas.

patterns.name: Ashoka's life and Dhamma
patterns.howToSpot: "Kalinga war year", "Devanampiya Piyadasi", "Dhamma Mahamattas", "Third Council".
steps: Kalinga war: 261 BCE, in his 8th regnal year.
Dhamma: a code of conduct, not a new religion.
Dhamma Mahamattas appear in RE V. He held the Third Buddhist Council.
patterns.why: Dhamma questions test whether you know it was ethics, not ritual.

example.q: In which year of his reign did Ashoka fight the Kalinga war?
steps: The war was in 261 BCE.
Ashoka fought it early in his reign.

patterns.name: Mauryan king and his faith
patterns.howToSpot: "Which king followed the Ajivikas", "became a Jain", "Amitraghata".
steps: Chandragupta: Jain at the end, with Bhadrabahu at Shravanabelagola.
Bindusara: Amitraghata, Ajivika follower.
Ashoka: Buddhist.
patterns.why: Each king has one faith, and the options swap them.

example.q: Which Mauryan king took the title Amitraghata?
steps: The title means slayer of foes.
He was Chandragupta's son.

revision: 322 BCE: Chandragupta and Chanakya end the Nandas. Megasthenes and Indica at his court.
Seleucus treaty 305 BCE: 500 elephants for eastern satrapies and a marriage alliance.
Kalinga 261 BCE led to Dhamma. Edicts in Prakrit and Brahmi. Prinsep deciphered them in 1837.
RE XIII Kalinga. RE XII tolerance. Bhabru Buddha-Dhamma-Sangha. Rummindei Lumbini.
Samaharta collects. Sannidhata is treasurer. Gudhapurushas are spies.
Lion Capital is the National Emblem. Barabar caves are Ajivika. Brihadratha fell in 185 BCE.

subtopics.title: Post-Mauryan Age: Shungas to Kushanas
subtopics.concept: After the Mauryas, north India saw the Shungas and Kanvas, while the Satavahanas ruled the Deccan. Groups from Central Asia also entered the north-west: Indo-Greeks, Shakas, Parthians and Kushanas. Kanishka was the greatest Kushana. Exams ask about rulers, coins, eras and Indo-Roman trade.

tricks.title: 57 minus, 78 plus
tricks.body: Vikram Samvat is **57 BCE**, so subtract. Shaka is **78 CE**, so add.

example.q: Shaka year 1948 matches which CE year?
steps: Add 78 to the Shaka year.

tricks.title: Satavahana: S-P-G-H
tricks.body: **S**imuka founder. **P**ratishthana capital. **G**autamiputra greatest. **H**ala poet.

mistakes.wrong: Giving Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription in Prakrit.
mistakes.right: Ashoka's edicts are Prakrit. Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription is in **Sanskrit**.

mistakes.wrong: Saying a Shaka ruler began the Shaka era.
mistakes.right: **Kanishka**, a Kushana, began it in 78 CE.

mistakes.wrong: Confusing Charaka with Sushruta.
mistakes.right: Charaka was Kanishka's physician. Sushruta is the surgeon.

mistakes.wrong: Placing the Kanvas before the Shungas.
mistakes.right: Order: Shunga (185 BCE), then Kanva (73 BCE).

subtopics.notes:
### Shungas and Kanvas
| Dynasty | Key facts |
|---|---|
| **Shunga** (c. 185 to 73 BCE) | **Pushyamitra Shunga** killed Brihadratha. He performed **2 Ashvamedhas**. **Patanjali** lived in his age. Agnimitra is the hero of Kalidasa's *Malavikagnimitram*. Bharhut stupa railings date here. |
| **Kanva** (c. 73 to 28 BCE) | **Vasudeva Kanva** killed the last Shunga king. The Satavahanas ended the Kanvas. |

### Foreign dynasties in the north-west
Learn them in order of arrival: Indo-Greeks, Shakas, Parthians, Kushanas.

| Group | Key ruler | Facts |
|---|---|---|
| **Indo-Greeks** | **Menander (Milinda)**, capital **Sakala (Sialkot)** | First coins with a king's portrait; *Milindapanha*; roots of Gandhara art |
| **Shakas** | **Rudradaman I** (Ujjain) | **Junagadh inscription**: first long inscription in chaste **Sanskrit**; repaired **Sudarshana lake** |
| **Parthians** | **Gondophernes** | Tradition links him with St. Thomas |
| **Kushanas** | Kujula Kadphises, Vima Kadphises, **Kanishka** | See below |

The Sudarshana lake was first built under Chandragupta Maurya's governor **Pushyagupta**.

### The Kushanas
**Vima Kadphises** issued large gold coins with Shiva on them.

**Kanishka** began the **Shaka era** in **78 CE**. It is the base of India's **National Calendar**.

- Capital: **Purushapura (Peshawar)**. Second centre: **Mathura**.
- He held the **Fourth Buddhist Council** at Kundalvana, Kashmir. He backed **Mahayana**.
- His court: **Ashvaghosha** (*Buddhacharita*), **Nagarjuna**, **Vasumitra**, physician **Charaka**.
- Two art schools grew. **Gandhara** used grey schist and a Greco-Roman style. **Mathura** used red sandstone and Indian style.

> **Watch:** The Shaka era was begun by Kanishka, a Kushana, not by a Shaka ruler.

### The Satavahanas
The Satavahanas ruled the Deccan. **Simuka** founded the dynasty. The capital was **Pratishthana (Paithan)** on the Godavari.

- **Gautamiputra Satakarni** was the greatest king. He destroyed the Kshaharata Shakas under **Nahapana**.
- His mother **Gautami Balashri**'s **Nasik inscription** praises him.
- **Hala** wrote *Gathasaptashati* in Prakrit.
- They gave the first **tax-free land grants to Brahmanas**.
- Their coins were of **lead** and potin. Their language was **Prakrit**.

**Kharavela** of Kalinga was a Jain patron. His record is the **Hathigumpha inscription** at Udayagiri, Odisha.

### Eras
| Era | Starts | Linked with |
|---|---|---|
| **Vikram Samvat** | **57 BCE** | Vikramaditya of Ujjain |
| **Shaka Samvat** | **78 CE** | **Kanishka** |
| Gupta era | 319 to 320 CE | Chandragupta I |
| Harsha era | 606 CE | Harshavardhana |

> **Tip:** Vikram Samvat: subtract 57 to get CE. Shaka: add 78.

### Indo-Roman trade
Yavana (Roman) traders came to Indian ports.

- **Tamralipti** in the east.
- **Bharuch** and **Sopara** in the west.
- **Muziris** in Kerala.
- **Arikamedu** near Pondicherry, where Roman pottery, lamps and beads were found.

Large hoards of **Roman gold coins** show that trade favoured India. The guide *Periplus of the Erythraean Sea* describes these ports.

patterns.name: Post-Mauryan dynasties and their kings
patterns.howToSpot: "Which dynasty came after the Shungas", "Rudradaman belonged to", or an order of dynasties.
steps: Heartland chain: Shunga, then Kanva.
North-west chain: Indo-Greeks, Shakas, Parthians, Kushanas.
King hooks: Menander Indo-Greek, Rudradaman Shaka, Gondophernes Parthian, Kanishka Kushana.
patterns.why: Each king has one dynasty, so the king names the dynasty.

example.q: Who repaired the Sudarshana lake and issued the first long inscription in chaste Sanskrit?
steps: The inscription is at Junagadh.
The Shaka ruler of Ujjain issued it.

patterns.name: Kanishka and the Kushanas
patterns.howToSpot: "The Shaka era was started by", Kanishka's capitals, Gandhara and Mathura art, scholars at his court.
steps: Kanishka: 78 CE Shaka era; Peshawar and Mathura.
He held the Fourth Council. Hinayana and Mahayana split.
Court: Ashvaghosha, Charaka, Vasumitra, Nagarjuna.
Art: Gandhara (grey schist) and Mathura (red sandstone).
patterns.why: Kanishka collects many separate facts, so the era and the capitals are the anchors.

example.q: Which Kushana ruler struck large gold issues showing Shiva on the coins?
steps: Kanishka's predecessor issued them.
He was Vima Kadphises.

patterns.name: Satavahanas: rulers, capital and customs
patterns.howToSpot: "Capital of the Satavahanas", Gautamiputra Satakarni, first land grants, lead coins.
steps: Founder Simuka. Capital Pratishthana (Paithan) on the Godavari.
Greatest king: Gautamiputra Satakarni. Evidence: the Nasik inscription of his mother.
Firsts: tax-free land grants to Brahmanas. Coins of lead and potin. Language Prakrit.
patterns.why: The Satavahana facts are few and fixed.

example.q: The greatest Satavahana ruler, whose deeds are told in his mother's Nasik inscription, was:
steps: His mother was Gautami Balashri.
His name begins with Gautami.

patterns.name: Indo-Roman trade
patterns.howToSpot: "Arikamedu is famous for", "the main east-coast port", Roman gold hoards, the Periplus.
steps: Ports: Tamralipti east; Bharuch and Sopara west; Muziris in Kerala; Arikamedu near Pondicherry.
Arikamedu gave Roman pottery, lamps and beads.
Roman gold hoards show a trade surplus for India.
patterns.why: Each port has one direction, so the direction helps.

example.q: Which post-Mauryan site near Pondicherry is famous for Roman pottery and trade goods?
steps: The site is on the south-east coast.
Its finds include Roman lamps and beads.

patterns.name: Eras and their founders
patterns.howToSpot: "Vikram Samvat began in", "Shaka era started in", "Gupta era", "Harsha era".
steps: Vikram Samvat 57 BCE. Shaka 78 CE. Gupta 319 to 320 CE. Harsha 606 CE.
To change a Vikram Samvat year to CE, subtract 57.
To change a Shaka year to CE, add 78.
patterns.why: Four dates cover all era questions.

example.q:
The Shaka Samvat, used in India's National Calendar, began in:
(a) 57 BCE (b) 78 CE (c) 319 CE (d) 606 CE
steps: 57 BCE is Vikram Samvat.
319 CE is the Gupta era and 606 CE the Harsha era.

revision: Heartland order: Shunga (185 to 73 BCE), then Kanva (73 to 28 BCE).
North-west order: Indo-Greeks, Shakas, Parthians, Kushanas.
Menander and Nagasena wrote the Milindapanha. Indo-Greeks gave the first portrait coins.
Rudradaman I: Junagadh inscription, chaste Sanskrit, Sudarshana lake.
Kanishka: Shaka era 78 CE, Peshawar and Mathura, Fourth Council, Gandhara and Mathura art.
Satavahanas: Simuka, Pratishthana, Gautamiputra Satakarni, first Brahmana land grants, lead coins.
Ports: Tamralipti, Bharuch, Sopara, Muziris. Arikamedu has Roman finds.

subtopics.title: Gupta Age & Harshavardhana
subtopics.concept: The Guptas ruled north India from about 320 CE and their age is called the classical or golden age. Harshavardhana was the last great northern king before the early medieval age. Exams ask about each ruler's title, scholars, books, Chinese pilgrims and Harsha's reign.

tricks.title: Gupta order
tricks.body: Sri Gupta, Ghatotkacha, then **Chandragupta I**, **Samudragupta**, **Chandragupta II**, **Kumaragupta I**, **Skandagupta**.

tricks.title: Inscription authors: H, R, B
tricks.body: **H**arishena wrote the Prayag Prashasti of Samudragupta. **R**avikirti wrote the Aihole inscription of Pulakeshin II. **B**anabhatta wrote Harsha's biography.

example.q: Who composed the Aihole inscription?
steps: Aihole belongs to Pulakeshin II.
Its poet was Ravikirti.

tricks.title: Pilgrims: F-H-I
tricks.body: Fa-Hien (Chandragupta II), then Hiuen Tsang (Harsha), then I-Tsing.

mistakes.wrong: Saying Fa-Hien came in Harsha's time.
mistakes.right: Fa-Hien came under **Chandragupta II**. Hiuen Tsang came under **Harsha**.

mistakes.wrong: Saying Harishena praised Chandragupta II.
mistakes.right: Harishena praised **Samudragupta**.

mistakes.wrong: Calling the Mehrauli Iron Pillar a Sultanate work.
mistakes.right: It is Gupta. It bears the name of king Chandra.

mistakes.wrong: Giving Aryabhata's birth year for the Aryabhatiya.
mistakes.right: Aryabhata was born in 476 CE. The *Aryabhatiya* is of 499 CE.

subtopics.notes:
### The Gupta line
| Ruler | Facts |
|---|---|
| Sri Gupta, Ghatotkacha | First two rulers |
| **Chandragupta I** | First *Maharajadhiraja*; married Licchavi princess **Kumaradevi**; **Gupta era 319 to 320 CE** |
| **Samudragupta** (c. 335 to 375) | **Prayag Prashasti** by **Harishena**; "**Napoleon of India**"; *Kaviraja* (veena on coins) |
| **Chandragupta II "Vikramaditya"** (c. 375 to 415) | Beat the Western Kshatrapas; **Navaratnas**; visited by **Fa-Hien**; Mehrauli Iron Pillar |
| **Kumaragupta I** | Founded **Nalanda** |
| **Skandagupta** | Stopped the **Hunas**; repaired **Sudarshana lake** |

The Prayag Prashasti is on the Allahabad pillar. It says Samudragupta uprooted nine kings of Aryavarta. It says he defeated but reinstated twelve rulers of Dakshinapatha.

Chandragupta II's daughter **Prabhavatigupta** married the Vakataka **Rudrasena II**. The Huns **Toramana** and **Mihirakula** came later. **Yashodharman** of Malwa defeated Mihirakula.

Gupta gold coins were called **dinaras**.

### Why it is called a golden age
**Science**

| Scholar | Work |
|---|---|
| **Aryabhata** | *Aryabhatiya* (499 CE): the earth rotates; eclipses come from shadows; place value |
| **Varahamihira** | *Brihat Samhita*, *Pancha Siddhantika* |
| **Brahmagupta** | *Brahmasphuta Siddhanta* (628 CE): rules for zero |
| Vagbhata | *Ashtanga Hridaya* (medicine) |

**Literature**

- **Kalidasa:** *Abhijnanashakuntalam*, *Meghaduta*, *Raghuvamsha*, *Kumarasambhava*, *Malavikagnimitram*.
- **Vishnu Sharma:** *Panchatantra*. **Amarasimha:** *Amarakosha*.
- **Dandin:** *Dashakumaracharita*. **Bharavi:** *Kiratarjuniya*.

**Art**

- **Dashavatara temple, Deogarh** shows an early shikhara.
- **Bhitargaon** brick temple, near Kanpur.
- **Udayagiri caves** near Vidisha have a Varaha panel.
- **Ajanta** murals reached their peak.

> **Watch:** Fa-Hien noted untouchability. The Eran inscription (510 CE) gives the first proof of sati.

### Chinese pilgrims
| Pilgrim | Years | Ruler | Book |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Fa-Hien** | 399 to 414 CE | Chandragupta II | *Fo-kwo-ki* |
| **Hiuen Tsang** | c. 630 to 645 CE | Harsha | *Si-Yu-Ki* |
| **I-Tsing** | 671 to 695 CE | After Harsha | Studied at Nalanda |

> **Tip:** F-H-I: Fa-Hien, Hiuen Tsang, I-Tsing. This is alphabetical and also the order in time.

### Harshavardhana
Harsha ruled from **606 to 647 CE**. He belonged to the **Pushyabhuti (Vardhana)** house of **Thanesar**. He moved his capital to **Kannauj**. The **Harsha era** starts in 606 CE.

- **Banabhatta** wrote *Harshacharita* and *Kadambari*.
- Harsha wrote three plays: *Nagananda*, *Ratnavali*, *Priyadarshika*.
- **Pulakeshin II** stopped him on the **Narmada**. The Aihole inscription by **Ravikirti** records this.
- He held an assembly at **Kannauj** in 643 CE to honour Hiuen Tsang.
- Every five years he held the **Prayag** assembly (*Mahamoksha Parishad*).

Hiuen Tsang studied at Nalanda and was called the "Prince of Pilgrims".

patterns.name: Gupta ruler and achievement or title
patterns.howToSpot: "Napoleon of India", who defeated the Shakas or Huns, Prashasti facts, founder of Nalanda.
steps: Samudragupta: Prayag Prashasti, Kaviraja, Napoleon of India.
Chandragupta II: Vikramaditya, beat the Western Shakas, Navaratnas.
Kumaragupta I: Nalanda. Skandagupta: Huns and Sudarshana lake.
patterns.why: Each ruler has one clear title or deed.

example.q: Which Gupta ruler took the title Vikramaditya after destroying the Western Shakas?
steps: Fa-Hien visited during his reign.
He was the son of Samudragupta.

patterns.name: Science and literature of the Gupta age
patterns.howToSpot: "The Aryabhatiya was written by", "which work is by Kalidasa", author pairs.
steps: Science: Aryabhata (Aryabhatiya), Varahamihira (Brihat Samhita).
Kalidasa: Shakuntalam, Meghaduta, Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava, Malavikagnimitram.
Pairs: Panchatantra-Vishnu Sharma, Amarakosha-Amarasimha, Dashakumaracharita-Dandin, Kiratarjuniya-Bharavi.
patterns.why: Setters use only these author and book pairs.

example.q: The Panchatantra, a collection of animal fables, is attributed to:
steps: It is a Sanskrit fable book.
Its author's name begins with Vishnu.

patterns.name: Harsha: capital, assemblies and court
patterns.howToSpot: Kannauj, Banabhatta, Harsha's plays, the Kannauj and Prayag assemblies, defeat on the Narmada.
steps: Harsha of Thanesar ruled from Kannauj; title Siladitya.
Banabhatta wrote Harshacharita and Kadambari. Harsha wrote Nagananda, Ratnavali, Priyadarshika.
Assemblies at Kannauj and Prayag. Pulakeshin II checked him on the Narmada.
patterns.why: Harsha's facts come in small sets of two or three.

example.q: Harshavardhana shifted his capital from Thanesar to:
steps: The new capital became the prize of later struggles.
It is Kannauj.

patterns.name: Visitors and the rulers they met
patterns.howToSpot: Match Megasthenes, Fa-Hien, Hiuen Tsang, I-Tsing (and Deimachus, Dionysius) to the courts they saw.
steps: Megasthenes with Chandragupta Maurya. Deimachus with Bindusara. Dionysius with Ashoka.
Fa-Hien with Chandragupta II. Hiuen Tsang with Harsha. I-Tsing after Harsha.
Books: Indica (Megasthenes), Si-Yu-Ki (Hiuen Tsang).
patterns.why: One list of visitor and ruler pairs answers every match question.

example.q: Which Chinese pilgrim visited India after Harsha's death and studied in its monasteries from 671 to 695?
steps: Fa-Hien came in the Gupta age.
Hiuen Tsang came in Harsha's reign.

patterns.name: Gupta art, coins and temples
patterns.howToSpot: "Dashavatara temple", "dinara", "Udayagiri", "Bhitargaon", "Ajanta".
steps: Dashavatara temple is at Deogarh. Bhitargaon is a brick temple.
Udayagiri caves (Vidisha) have the Varaha panel.
Gupta gold coins were dinaras.
patterns.why: Each site has one signature feature.

example.q: Gupta gold coins were known as:
steps: The name is like the Roman denarius.
The Gupta term is dinara.

patterns.name: Dark side of the golden age
patterns.howToSpot: "First epigraphic proof of sati", "untouchability noted by", "status of women".
steps: Eran inscription, 510 CE: first proof of sati.
Fa-Hien noted untouchability.
Women's status fell in this age.
patterns.why: Setters use the golden-age label to trap you with the negatives.

example.q: The first epigraphic proof of sati comes from which Gupta-age inscription?
steps: The site is in central India.
The year is 510 CE.

revision: Chain: Chandragupta I, Samudragupta, Chandragupta II, Kumaragupta I, Skandagupta.
Samudragupta: Prayag Prashasti by Harishena, Napoleon of India, Kaviraja.
Chandragupta II: Vikramaditya, beat the Shakas, Navaratnas with Kalidasa, Fa-Hien.
Kumaragupta I founded Nalanda. Skandagupta stopped the Huns and repaired Sudarshana lake.
Aryabhata wrote the Aryabhatiya. Varahamihira wrote the Brihat Samhita.
Harsha: Thanesar, then Kannauj; Banabhatta; three plays; stopped by Pulakeshin II.

subtopics.title: Sangam Age & South Indian Dynasties
subtopics.concept: South India had the Sangam kingdoms of Chera, Chola and Pandya, then the Pallavas, Chalukyas, Rashtrakutas and Imperial Cholas. Each dynasty is remembered for its rulers, capital, temples and literature. Exams ask you to match dynasty, king, monument and emblem.

tricks.title: B-T-F
tricks.body: Chera **B**ow, Chola **T**iger, Pandya **F**ish.

tricks.title: Imperial Cholas: V-P-R-R
tricks.body: Vijayalaya, Parantaka, Rajaraja, Rajendra.

mistakes.wrong: Saying Rajaraja I built the Kailasa temple.
mistakes.right: Kailasa (Ellora) is Rashtrakuta. Rajaraja I built the Brihadeeswara temple.

mistakes.wrong: Calling the Shore Temple Chola.
mistakes.right: The Shore Temple is Pallava, built by Rajasimha.

mistakes.wrong: Giving the Chera emblem as fish.
mistakes.right: Fish is Pandya. Chera has the bow.

mistakes.wrong: Confusing Aihole with Ellora.
mistakes.right: Aihole and Pattadakal are Chalukya. Ellora Kailasa is Rashtrakuta.

subtopics.notes:
### The Sangam kingdoms
| Kingdom | Capital and port | Emblem | Famous king |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Chera** | **Vanji**; ports **Muziris** and **Tondi** | **Bow** | **Senguttuvan** |
| **Chola** | **Uraiyur**; port **Puhar** | **Tiger** | **Karikala**, built the **Kallanai** dam |
| **Pandya** | **Madurai**; port **Korkai** | **Fish** | **Nedunjeliyan** |

> **Tip:** Chera bow, Chola tiger, Pandya fish. The letters B-T-F give the order.

### Sangam literature
- **Tolkappiyam**: the oldest Tamil grammar.
- **Tirukkural** by **Thiruvalluvar**: couplets on ethics.
- **Silappadikaram** by **Ilango Adigal**. **Manimekalai** by **Sittalai Sattanar**.
- **Ettuthokai** and **Pattupattu**: the eight anthologies and ten idylls.
- Poems are of two kinds: **akam** (love) and **puram** (war and praise).

### Pallavas of Kanchi
- **Mahendravarman I** was a patron of rock-cut temples.
- **Narasimhavarman I "Mamalla"** took **Vatapi** and took the title **Vatapikonda**. Mamallapuram is his city.
- **Rajasimha** built the **Shore Temple** and the **Kailasanatha temple** at Kanchi.

Their style moved from rock-cut caves to monolithic *rathas* and then to structural temples.

### Chalukyas of Badami
**Pulakeshin II** stopped Harsha on the Narmada. His temples are at **Aihole** and **Pattadakal**.

### Rashtrakutas
**Krishna I** carved the **Kailasa temple** at **Ellora**. **Amoghavarsha** wrote *Kavirajamarga*, the first Kannada poetics work.

The **tripartite struggle** for **Kannauj** was among the **Palas**, **Pratiharas** and **Rashtrakutas**.

### Imperial Cholas
Order: **Vijayalaya** (founder, Thanjavur), then **Parantaka I**, then **Rajaraja I**, then **Rajendra I**.

- **Parantaka I**: the **Uttaramerur** inscriptions describe village self-government.
- **Rajaraja I** built the **Brihadeeswara temple**, Thanjavur.
- **Rajendra I** built a new capital and took Ganga water north.
- Local bodies were the **Ur**, **Sabha** and **Nagaram**. Members were chosen by **kudavolai** (a lot system).

The Chola temples at Thanjavur, Gangaikonda Cholapuram and Darasuram are **UNESCO** sites.

### Rulers to remember
| Dynasty | Founder or best-known king | Seat |
|---|---|---|
| Pallava | Mahendravarman I | Kanchi |
| Chalukya of Badami | Pulakeshin II | Badami (Vatapi) |
| Rashtrakuta | Krishna I | Manyakheta |
| Imperial Chola | Vijayalaya | Thanjavur |

Each dynasty has one signature monument. Learn the monument with the king.

### Temple styles
| Style | Region |
|---|---|
| **Nagara** | North India |
| **Dravida** | South India |
| **Vesara** | Deccan, a mix of both |

> **Rule:** Pallava, Chola and Pandya temples are Dravida. Chalukya temples show Vesara traits.

patterns.name: Sangam kingdoms: capital, port, emblem
patterns.howToSpot: "Emblem of the Pandyas", "capital of the Cheras", "port of the Cholas".
steps: Chera: Vanji, Muziris and Tondi, bow.
Chola: Uraiyur, Puhar, tiger.
Pandya: Madurai, Korkai, fish.
patterns.why: Each kingdom has a fixed set of capital, port and emblem.

example.q: Which Sangam kingdom had Madurai as its capital and the fish as its emblem?
steps: The fish is a Pandya emblem.
Madurai was its capital.

patterns.name: Sangam literature and authors
patterns.howToSpot: "Tirukkural was written by", "oldest Tamil grammar", Silappadikaram or Manimekalai.
steps: Tolkappiyam: grammar. Tirukkural: Thiruvalluvar.
Silappadikaram: Ilango Adigal. Manimekalai: Sittalai Sattanar.
Anthologies: Ettuthokai and Pattupattu.
patterns.why: Text and author pairs are fixed.

example.q: The Tamil epic Silappadikaram was composed by:
steps: The author was a Chera prince turned monk.
His name is Ilango Adigal.

patterns.name: Pallava, Chalukya and Rashtrakuta monuments
patterns.howToSpot: "Shore Temple", "Kailasa temple", "Aihole and Pattadakal", "Vatapikonda".
steps: Pallava: Mahendravarman I rock-cut, Mamalla rathas, Rajasimha Shore Temple and Kailasanatha.
Chalukya: Aihole and Pattadakal.
Rashtrakuta: Kailasa temple, Ellora, by Krishna I.
patterns.why: Every monument links to one dynasty and one king.

example.q: Which dynasty built the monolithic Kailasa temple at Ellora?
steps: It was carved in a single rock.
Krishna I was the king.

patterns.name: Imperial Cholas and local government
patterns.howToSpot: "Brihadeeswara temple builder", Uttaramerur, Ur and Sabha, kudavolai.
steps: Founder Vijayalaya. Then Parantaka I, Rajaraja I, Rajendra I.
Rajaraja I: Brihadeeswara, Thanjavur.
Local bodies: Ur, Sabha, Nagaram. The Uttaramerur inscriptions of Parantaka I describe them.
patterns.why: The Chola chain and its local-government terms answer most questions.

example.q: The Uttaramerur inscriptions of Parantaka I describe:
steps: They are on a temple wall in Tamil Nadu.
They tell how village bodies were chosen.
example.answer: Village self-government (Sabha members chosen by lot)

patterns.name: Temple styles and the tripartite struggle
patterns.howToSpot: "Nagara, Dravida, Vesara", "struggle for Kannauj".
steps: Nagara: north. Dravida: south. Vesara: Deccan mix.
Tripartite struggle: Palas, Pratiharas, Rashtrakutas.
The prize was Kannauj.
patterns.why: Style names and struggle names are asked as short lists.

example.q: The tripartite struggle for Kannauj involved the Palas, Rashtrakutas and:
steps: The third power ruled from the west and north.
It began with the letter P.

revision: Sangam: Chera (Vanji, bow), Chola (Uraiyur, tiger), Pandya (Madurai, fish).
Tolkappiyam is the grammar. Tirukkural is by Thiruvalluvar.
Pallavas: Mahendravarman I, Narasimhavarman I Mamalla, Rajasimha (Shore Temple, Kailasanatha).
Chalukyas of Badami: Pulakeshin II, Aihole and Pattadakal.
Rashtrakutas: Krishna I (Kailasa, Ellora), Amoghavarsha (Kavirajamarga).
Imperial Cholas: Vijayalaya, Parantaka I, Rajaraja I, Rajendra I.
Tripartite struggle: Palas, Pratiharas, Rashtrakutas for Kannauj.

subtopics.title: Ancient Literature & Authors
subtopics.concept: Ancient Indian literature includes Sanskrit epics and plays, Pali and Ardhamagadhi religious texts and Tamil Sangam works. Foreign accounts and inscriptions add to the record. Exams mostly ask you to match a book with its author.

tricks.title: Kalidasa's three K-words
tricks.body: Kalidasa wrote **M**eghaduta, **R**aghuvamsha, **K**umarasambhava, **S**hakuntalam. Shakuntalam is his most famous play.

tricks.title: Two chroniclers
tricks.body: **Kalhana** wrote the history of Kashmir. **Banabhatta** wrote Harsha's life.

mistakes.wrong: Giving Kautilya as author of the Mudrarakshasa.
mistakes.right: Kautilya wrote the Arthashastra. **Vishakhadatta** wrote the Mudrarakshasa.

mistakes.wrong: Attributing Panchatantra to Narayana Pandit.
mistakes.right: Panchatantra is by **Vishnu Sharma**. Narayana Pandit wrote the Hitopadesha.

mistakes.wrong: Confusing Charaka and Sushruta.
mistakes.right: Charaka is for medicine. Sushruta is for surgery.

mistakes.wrong: Placing Prinsep's decipherment of Brahmi before 1800.
mistakes.right: Prinsep deciphered Brahmi in 1837.

subtopics.notes:
### Sanskrit works and authors
| Work | Author |
|---|---|
| *Ramayana* | **Valmiki** |
| *Mahabharata* | **Vyasa** |
| *Ashtadhyayi* | **Panini** |
| *Mahabhashya* | **Patanjali** |
| *Arthashastra* | **Kautilya** |
| *Natyashastra* | **Bharata** |
| *Buddhacharita* | **Ashvaghosha** |
| *Shakuntalam*, *Meghaduta*, *Raghuvamsha* | **Kalidasa** |
| *Mudrarakshasa* | **Vishakhadatta** |
| *Mrichchhakatika* | **Shudraka** |
| *Swapnavasavadatta* | **Bhasa** |
| *Kamasutra* | **Vatsyayana** |
| *Panchatantra* | **Vishnu Sharma** |
| *Hitopadesha* | **Narayana Pandit** |
| *Amarakosha* | **Amarasimha** |
| *Harshacharita*, *Kadambari* | **Banabhatta** |
| *Kiratarjuniya* | **Bharavi** |
| *Shishupalavadha* | **Magha** |
| *Dashakumaracharita* | **Dandin** |
| *Rajatarangini* | **Kalhana** |
| *Brihatkatha* | **Gunadhya** |

> **Note:** *Manusmriti* is a law text. *Rajatarangini* is the first history book of Kashmir.

### Science and medicine
- **Charaka** wrote on medicine.
- **Sushruta** wrote on surgery.
- **Aryabhata**, **Varahamihira** and **Brahmagupta** wrote on astronomy and maths.
- **Vagbhata** wrote *Ashtanga Hridaya*.

### Religious literature
- The Buddhist canon is the **Tripitaka**, in **Pali**.
- The Jain canon is in **Ardhamagadhi**.
- **Deepavamsha** and **Mahavamsha** are Sri Lankan chronicles that mention Ashoka.

### Foreign accounts
| Source | Author |
|---|---|
| *Indica* | **Megasthenes** |
| *Fo-kwo-ki* | **Fa-Hien** |
| *Si-Yu-Ki* | **Hiuen Tsang** |
| *Periplus of the Erythraean Sea* | Unknown Greek sailor |

Pliny and Ptolemy also described India.

### Other texts to know
| Text | Note |
|---|---|
| *Manusmriti* | Law text of the Manu tradition |
| *Milindapanha* | Dialogue of Menander and the monk Nagasena |
| *Gathasaptashati* | Prakrit verses by the Satavahana king **Hala** |
| *Kavirajamarga* | Early Kannada poetics by **Amoghavarsha** |
| *Tirukkural* | Tamil couplets by **Thiruvalluvar** |
| *Silappadikaram* | Tamil epic by **Ilango Adigal** |

The Vedas, Brahmanas, Upanishads and Puranas are religious and philosophical texts. Use them with care as history.

> **Watch:** A Sangam text is Tamil. A Pali text is Buddhist. Do not mix the language with the region.

### Inscriptions and coins
**James Prinsep** deciphered **Brahmi** in **1837**. The **Hathigumpha** inscription tells of **Kharavela**.

> **Tip:** Coin ladder: punch-marked coins came first. The Indo-Greeks issued portrait coins. The Kushanas issued gold. The Guptas issued dinaras.
